page.metaTitle: Black Friday Deal Tracking & Price Alerts | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Track Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals across Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and any retailer. Set price thresholds, get alerts the moment deals drop.
page.subtitle: Set up monitors before Thanksgiving week, get alerts the moment a deal hits your threshold. Covers Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Costco — any retailer with a public product page.
page.intro: Black Friday and the week leading into it produce more flash deals than any other shopping window of the year. Manual deal-watching means refreshing tabs and missing half the drops. WebMonitor.fyi runs the polling for you on five-minute intervals during the Black Friday window so the alert arrives within five minutes of the deal posting.

setup.title: Build the wishlist before Thanksgiving
setup.body: Start adding product URLs the week before. Trying to set up 20 monitors during the Friday morning rush is exactly when you don't want to be in the dashboard.

setup.title: Set a target price per item
setup.body: For each monitor, the criterion: "alert me when this drops below $X" or "notify me when this is at least 30% off". Specific thresholds beat "any change" — fewer false alerts.

setup.title: Bump frequency to five minutes from Thanksgiving night
setup.body: The dashboard lets you adjust per-monitor frequency. Bump high-priority items to five-minute intervals starting Thanksgiving evening through Cyber Monday midnight.

setup.title: Route alerts to SMS for the high-stakes items
setup.body: Email and Slack are fine for everyday tracking. For limited-stock items that sell out in minutes, SMS gets the alert in front of you fastest.

examples: A laptop you've been waiting on — alert when it drops below $X

Tracking lightning-deal pages where products rotate every few hours
page.limits: During peak Black Friday traffic, some retailers throttle product pages or briefly serve cached versions. Monitors are still reliable, but a 5-minute interval might effectively become a 6–8 minute interval if the retailer is rate-limiting. Plan accordingly for the highest-stakes items.

faq.q: When should I set up Black Friday monitors?
faq.a: The week before Thanksgiving is the right window. Many retailers start dropping early Black Friday deals 10–14 days ahead, so monitors set up that early catch the early drops too.

faq.q: Will the monitors keep working through Cyber Monday?
faq.a: Yes. Monitors run continuously until you pause or delete them. Cyber Monday extends the deal window — many of the best electronics deals show up Sunday night into Monday.

faq.q: Can I track competitor pricing during Black Friday too?
faq.a: Yes — many e-commerce brands use Black Friday weekend specifically to watch competitor pricing for next-year planning. Set monitors on competitor pricing pages for the weekend.

faq.q: What happens to my monitors after Cyber Monday?
faq.a: They keep running until you change them. Many users bump the frequency back to hourly or daily after the weekend and leave the monitors as ongoing trackers for the next shopping cycle.
